# Use design-doc

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Generate a Google-style engineering design doc (problem, goals/non-goals, options considered, recommended approach, risks, rollout) from a feature brief or short description.

**Reach for it when** the user wants to draft a design doc, technical proposal, or one-pager for an engineering review.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install design-doc                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install design-doc --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install design-doc --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Solution architect pack: [`--pack solution-architect`](../packs/use-the-solution-architect-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Draft a design doc for this feature"
- "Write a Google-style engineering design document from this brief"
- "I need a technical design with goals, non-goals, alternatives, and rollout"
- "Turn this feature brief into a design doc the team can review"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Write an ADR recording this one decision"
- "Draft the product requirements document for this feature"
- "Critique the design doc I already wrote"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use design-doc".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Non-goals are real, not throat-clearing.** If your non-goals list reads "we're not solving world hunger", delete it. Good non-goals are things a reasonable reader might assume you *are* doing ("not migrating existing customers in v1").
- **Alternatives have a why-not, not just a description.** Two sentences each: what is it, why didn't we pick it.
- **Risks have mitigations.** A bare list of "things that could go wrong" is anxiety, not engineering.
- **Rollout criteria are concrete.** "We'll monitor closely" is not a criterion. "Roll forward to 100% if p99 < 80ms for 48h after 10% rollout" is.
